title: Agent Action Record
description: A single tamper-evident ledger entry describing one consequential action taken by an AI agent: who acted, under what policy, on what evidence, approved by whom, with what outcome. Records are append-only and hash-chained.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. Consumers must reject records whose major version they do not understand.

record_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this record. Immutable once written.

incident_id.description: Correlation key tying every record of one incident together (investigate -> propose_fix -> approve -> execute -> outcome). Required so an auditor can reconstruct a complete chain without inferring it from timestamps.

in_response_to.description: record_id of the record that directly caused this one, e.g. an approve record points at the request_approval it answers, and an execute record points at the approve that authorized it. Absent on the first record of an incident.

timestamp.description: When the action occurred, ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset (Z). Not when the record was written.

actor.description: The agent or system that performed the action. For human-performed actions (approve/reject) the actor is still the platform that recorded it; the human is named in `approver`.

agent_name.description: Logical name of the acting agent, e.g. 'holmesgpt-investigator'.

agent_version.description: Version of the agent. Pin this precisely enough to reproduce behaviour: a release tag or commit sha, not 'latest'.

tool_or_platform.description: The underlying platform that executed the agent, e.g. 'holmesgpt'. This is the vendor-neutral join key across agent vendors.

invocation_id.description: Identifier of the single agent run that produced this action. All records from one HolmesGPT invocation share it.

model.description: Underlying LLM that produced the reasoning, when applicable. Auditors ask this; capture it when the platform exposes it.

action_type.description: What kind of consequential action this record captures.

summary.description: One-line human-readable statement of what happened, written so a compliance reviewer understands the record without decoding the structured fields.

target.description: The resource the action was taken against or about.

resource_id.description: Stable identifier of the resource within its environment, e.g. 'default/checkout-api' or 'orders-db/primary'.

environment.description: Deployment environment. Drives policy: production actions demand stricter approval.

policy_reference.description: The specific rule that permitted this action. A record that only says 'RBAC allowed it' is not auditable; `allowed_by` must name a concrete rule or declare a human override.

policy_id.description: Stable identifier of the policy document and version, e.g. 'sre-agent-policy-v3'.

policy_description.description: Human-readable statement of what the policy permits, quoted closely enough that a reviewer need not open the policy document.

allowed_by.description: The named rule within the policy that authorized this action, e.g. 'rule:read_only_investigation'. The literal 'human_override' is permitted only when a named human accepted responsibility, in which case `approver` must be present and of type 'human'.

policy_digest.description: sha256 of the exact policy document text in force at the time. Proves which wording was actually applied, even if the policy is later edited.

evidence.description: Everything the actor looked at to justify this action. An action with no evidence is permitted only for purely procedural records; investigate and propose_fix records must cite at least one item.

proposed_action.description: The concrete change being proposed or executed. Required on propose_fix and execute records so that 'what did it propose' and 'what did it actually do' are answerable without reading prose.

description.description: Plain-language statement of the intended change and why it addresses the finding.

change_type.description: Category of change, used to route approval requirements.

command_or_diff.description: The exact command, patch or manifest diff that will be applied. Recorded verbatim so the approver approves the real thing, not a paraphrase.

reversible.description: Whether the change can be undone by a rollback action without data loss.

blast_radius.description: Reviewer-facing estimate of how much is affected if this goes wrong.

approver.description: Who authorized the action. Null on records that need no authorization (investigations, and the proposal itself). Must be populated on approve, reject, and on any execute of a production-affecting change.

approver_id.description: Identity of the approver, resolvable to a real person or to the policy that auto-approved. Not a display name alone.

approver_type.description: Whether a human accepted responsibility or a policy rule auto-approved.

approved_at.description: When the approval decision was made, ISO 8601 UTC.

approval_channel.description: Where the decision was captured, e.g. 'cli', 'web_dashboard', 'slack'. Tells an auditor where to find corroborating logs.

approver_display_name.description: Human-friendly name for dashboard display. Never the sole identifier.

decision_note.description: Free-text rationale the approver gave at decision time.

status.description: 'pending' is legitimate and expected on request_approval records; it must be resolved by a later record in the chain, never by mutating this one.

details.description: What actually happened, including error text on failure.

duration_ms.description: How long the action took, where measurable.

prev_record_hash.description: record_hash of the immediately preceding record in the ledger. The genesis record uses 64 zeros. This is what makes deletion and reordering detectable.

record_hash.description: sha256 over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of this record with the record_hash field itself removed. Because prev_record_hash is part of the hashed content, altering any earlier record breaks every hash after it.

evidence_item.description: One artifact the actor consulted. Immutable once the record is written: inline content is covered by record_hash, blob content is content-addressed by its own sha256.

evidence_type.description: What kind of artifact this is.

source.description: Where it came from, precisely enough to re-run: a query string, an endpoint, a file path, or a git ref.

snapshot_ref_or_inline.description: The evidence content itself, held inline when small or as a content-addressed blob when large.

retrieved_at.description: When the evidence was captured, ISO 8601 UTC. May precede the record timestamp.

redacted.description: True when content was scrubbed before storage, e.g. a leaked secret replaced by a placeholder. Auditors must be able to tell redaction from absence.

evidence_inline.description: Evidence small enough to live in the record. Its integrity is guaranteed by record_hash.

content_type.description: IANA media type of the content, e.g. 'text/plain', 'application/json'.

content.description: The evidence verbatim. Keep under 8 KiB; larger artifacts belong in a blob.

truncated.description: True when this inline copy is an excerpt of a larger artifact.

evidence_blob.description: Evidence held in content-addressed object storage. The sha256 is both the integrity proof and the storage key, so the blob cannot be swapped without detection.

content_type.description: IANA media type of the stored blob.

sha256.description: sha256 of the blob bytes. Also its filename in the store.

uri.description: Where to fetch the blob, e.g. 'file://evidence_store/ab/abcd...' or an s3:// URL.

size_bytes.description: Size of the blob in bytes.

preview.description: Short excerpt rendered in the dashboard so a reviewer need not download the blob to get the gist.

allOf.description: A proposed fix must state the concrete change and cite the evidence behind it.
An investigation must record what it looked at, otherwise it proves nothing.
Approve and reject records must name the decision-maker and answer a specific prior request.
An execution must state what it ran and point at the approval that authorized it. This is the rule that makes silent auto-remediation impossible to record as compliant.
A human_override must name the human who took responsibility.
